chunks: "The thief's hand is cut off for everything whose value reaches one-fifth of a dinar, even if he stole from a market, a field, or other than that."

So the proper way regarding these reports is that we carry them upon a kind of taqiyyah, because they agree with the doctrine of some of the generality. And it is possible that these reports are specific to one regarding whose condition the Imam sees that the public interest requires cutting his hand for property of this value, because that is among his duties which he himself undertakes, or one whom he commands undertakes it. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:
And from him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: prudential dissimulation or precautionary conformity in expression
key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief subject to the legal ruling discussed here
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the Imam, who determines and carries out certain legal duties
key_terms.الْمَصْلَحَةَ: the public interest or welfare considered in applying the ruling
key_terms.خُمُسَ دِينَارٍ: one-fifth of a dinar, the stated monetary threshold
key_terms.فَرَائِضِهِ: his obligatory duties or prescribed responsibilities
key_terms.قَطْعَ يَدِهِ: cutting his hand, the hadd punishment under discussion

ai.seo_question: How are reports about cutting the thief's hand at one-fifth of a dinar understood in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This passage discusses reports concerning the hadd punishment for theft when the stolen property's value reaches one-fifth of a dinar. It explains that such reports may be understood as issued under taqiyyah or as cases restricted to the Imam's discretionary judgment in view of public interest and his governing authority.
